about: The inputs the other six files never send.
Every other vector file is well-formed on purpose, and that turned out to
be a blind spot with a shape: three real divergences got in through it.
A duplicated level name made `rank` return the FIRST index in Rust and the
LAST in TypeScript — same input, two answers — and in TypeScript that broke
`pack`/`unpack` being inverse. A single NaN sailed through both closure
checks in a breakdown, because every comparison with NaN is false including
the ones meant to reject it.
JSON has no NaN or Infinity literal, so they are written as the strings
"NaN" and "Infinity" and each runner converts. A vector that cannot
express the value it is testing is not testing it.
WIDTH IS NOT HERE ON PURPOSE. Rust packs 64 debits and TypeScript 32,
because JavaScript's bitwise operators are 32-bit. That is a capability
difference, not a conformance failure — both refuse rather than truncate,
and a shared vector at 33 levels would fail a correct implementation.

coverage.criterion: every refusal a carrier or a breakdown can produce, plus the two degenerate carriers that are still valid
coverage.why: refusals are enumerated from the error type, so a failure mode nobody thought to name is not here either

cases.name: one level is degenerate but valid
two levels is the shortest carrier that says anything
a mass that is not a number
a price that is not finite
a piece was dropped, so the masses do not close
the masses close but the pieces rebuild a different total
nothing at all is not a breakdown either
